newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end little changed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end little changed in dull trade.

text.p: Indian blue chips closed mixed in dull trade on Monday, with the focus on select stocks ahead of an impending hike in petroleum product prices, dealers said.
"The market was steady today. Some profit-taking eroded mid-session gains," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani in Bombay.
A market holiday in Hong Kong affected institutional business, but some foreign funds were bidders in select stocks, traders said.
Tractor and utility maker, Mahindra & Mahindra rose 7.0 rupees up at 343.75 ahead of its annual results due on Tuesday.

Analysts said they expected Mahindra's net to climb nearly 21 percent to an average 2.03 billion rupees (US$56.7 million) in 1996/97, from 1.68 billion the previous year on the back of strong growth in rural disposable incomes.
Funds were buyers in HPCL, BPCL -- oil and refinery stocks, ICICI, IDBI -- financial institutions and Infosys, Satyam Computers and Tata Infotech -- software stocks, participants said.
Oil and refinery shares have provided a defensive hedge against the negative impact of impending petroleum product price rises on stock markets, analysts said.
A fall in Indian interest rates in the last few months had attracted fund buying in development financial institutions, analysts said.
Tata Infotech hit a daily price limit of 10 percent at 911.0 rupees, surging 82.75 rupees after the firm said its board of directors will meet on June 13 to finalise a bonus share issue.

Infosys Technnologies jumped 99.25 rupees or 6.4 percent, to 1,640.50 after its board said on Saturday it had approved an increase in foreign institutional investors holding limit to 30 percent from 24 percent, traders said.
